page: Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is a general-purpose virtual machine instance belonging to the c3 server family. It features 4 vCPUs mapped to 2 physical cores of an Intel Xeon 8481C processor running at 2.7 GHz, with 2 threads per core. The instance is equipped with 16.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. It utilizes the x86_64 architecture and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. No local storage or GPUs are bundled with this instance, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

The processor supports advanced instruction sets, including Intel Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX, AVX512F, AVX512_VNNI, AVX_VNNI, AVX512_BF16) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX_TILE, AMX_INT8), alongside cryptographic acceleration flags like AES, VAES, and SHA_NI. In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates average single-core performance, with a stress-ng single-core score of 1618.89 and a Geekbench single-core score of 1713.0. However, multi-core performance is relatively weak, as shown by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3315.66 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 3813.0. Memory bandwidth is also in the lower tier, with uncached large-block read speeds of 28.42 GB/sec and write speeds of 21.13 GB/sec.

Given its balanced 1:4 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, the c3-standard-4 is designed for general-purpose workloads. It achieves average throughput in static web serving (6.68 GB/sec) and single-threaded operations like gzip compression (26.37 GB/sec) and bzip3 decompression (11.4 GB/sec). However, it exhibits weak performance in database operations, software compilation, and multi-threaded decompression. While the inclusion of AMX and AVX-512 instructions provides hardware-level acceleration for specific vector and matrix operations, the overall resource density and lower multi-core benchmark results suggest this instance is best suited for moderate web serving, basic text processing, and lightweight single-threaded tasks rather than highly parallelized or memory-intensive database workloads.
description: The Google Cloud Platform c3-standard-4 is a general-purpose instance featuring 4 vCPUs and 16.0 GB of RAM, powered by a 2.7 GHz Intel Xeon 8481C processor with 2 physical cores and 2 threads per core. Built on the x86_64 architecture, it includes advanced instruction sets like AVX-512 and Intel AMX for matrix operations, but lacks bundled local storage and GPUs. Performance benchmarks indicate average single-core capabilities, with a Geekbench single-core score of 1713.0 and a static web serving throughput of 6.68 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are relatively weak, as evidenced by a stress-ng multi-core score of 3315.66 and uncached read speeds of 28.42 GB/sec. This hardware profile makes the instance qualitatively cost-effective for moderate, single-threaded applications, basic text processing, and web serving, while representing a performance tradeoff for highly parallelized database operations or intensive software compilation.
